title: Notice of Intent for the Department of Transportation (DOT) to Implement Executive Order 14398 � Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors
description: Notice of Intent for the Department of Transportation (DOT) to Implement Executive Order 14398 � Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL Consistent with Administration priorities and applicable law, the Department of Transportation (DOT) hereby provides notice of its intent to take immediate action to implement Executive Order (E.O.) 14398, Addressing DEI Discrimination by Federal Contractors (March 26, 2026). E.O. 14398 establishes that Federal agencies shall not do business with contractors that engage in racially discriminatory diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) activities. On April 20, 2026, the Federal Acquisition Regulatory (FAR) Council issued model deviation text to implement E.O. 14398, directing agencies to update their Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) class deviations for FAR Parts 9, 12, 22, and 52. In alignment with this direction, DOT issued FAR Class Deviation 2026-24 on April 24, 2026, implementing the required changes pending formal FAR rulemaking. Effective immediately, Contracting Officers shall insert the required E.O. 14398 clause in all new solicitations and resulting contracts valued above the micro-purchase threshold, including those for commercial products and commercial services, where the place of delivery or performance is in the United States. DOT is concurrently updating its existing contract portfolio to incorporate the requirements of E.O. 14398. Contracting Officers shall make every effort to bilaterally modify existing contracts no later than July 24, 2026. DOT is implementing E.O. 14398 as a matter of policy and compliance. Contractors seeking to compete for, or continue performing, DOT contracts should ensure alignment with E.O. 14398 and associated requirements.

The objectives of this initiative are to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire by accelerating and expanding forest restoration treatments and to bolster the region�s wood utilization capacity by providing a consistent supply of wood products. Project Overview and Scope: Approximately 13,000 acres is planned for treatment across the Bitterroot Front Planning Area over a 10?year period, with the potential to add more acres adjacent to the planning area. A minimum of 90,000 CCF (approximately 45 million board feet) of commercial timber is anticipated to be offered over the contract life; volumes may fluctuate annually. Types of Service Work contemplated include: Road maintenance, reconditioning, construction, and decommissioning. Reconstruction plans and design are not contemplated to be activities. Timber removal including logging and transportation. Timber sale preparation activities which include harvest unit layout, GPS traversing, unit boundary marking, interior marking and cruising. Biomass removal including thinning non-merchantable material, slashing, chipping, staging, transportation and other related activities. Road maintenance and reconstruction activities may be priced by the mile or contract quantity. If transportation of forest products is a service item, delivered tons or CCF are anticipated to be used. Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive prices at the task order level as projects are solicited. Project Overview and Scope: Approximately 13,000 acres is planned for treatment across the Bitterroot Front Planning Area over a 10?year period, with the potential to add more acres adjacent to the planning area. Four project areas may be offered at contract award for immediate implementation. Additional project areas are planned to be offered on an annual basis subject to funding. Two project areas may be offered for timber sale layout at the start of this project. A minimum of 90,000 CCF (approximately 45 million board feet) of commercial timber is anticipated to be offered over the contract life; volumes may fluctuate annually. Types of Service Work contemplated include: Road maintenance, reconditioning, construction, and decommissioning. Reconstruction plans and design are not contemplated to be activities. Timber removal including logging and transportation. Timber sale preparation activities which include harvest unit layout, GPS traversing, unit boundary marking, interior marking and cruising. Biomass removal including thinning non-merchantable material, slashing, chipping, staging, transportation and other related activities. Anticipated Terms: Minimum timber value estimates will be based on base rates and/or appraised rates if appropriate as determined from the Forest Service�s Timber appraisal system.?Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive pricing on offered forest products at the task order level as projects are issued. Payment terms for service work items are anticipated to be by the acre or linear foot for most treatments. Road maintenance and reconstruction activities may be priced by the mile or contract quantity. If transportation of forest products is a service item, delivered tons or CCF are anticipated to be used. Offerors will have the opportunity to provide competitive prices at the task order level as projects are solicited. The projects may include both mandatory and optional service items; product value at awarded rates will be used to offset the cost-of-service work items. Davis-Bacon wages and certified payrolls will be required for all Road Construction requirements. Service Contract Act wages will apply towards all non-construction service work requirements. Road construction requirements will be subject to bonding at applicable regulatory thresholds. Depending on the scale of scope in task orders, 3-5 year periods of performance are contemplated. A site visit is scheduled for October 28, 2025, to discuss the project in detail and share information. There is no planned virtual option for this site visit at this time. title: Turnkey Event Management and Production Services for the American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice only. The solicitation is not available at this time. Quotations submitted in response to this notice will not be accepted. The U.S. Department of State, U.S. Embassy Singapore, intends to issue a Request for Quotations for turnkey event planning, production, and management services for the inaugural American Thanksgiving in Singapore Festival. The public festival is tentatively planned for November 2026 at Jewel Changi Airport, Level 4. The event will be designed to accommodate an anticipated attendance of at least 1,000 people. It is expected to include multiple activity zones, American corporate partners, exhibitors, entertainment, food and beverage activations, and interactive experiences highlighting American Thanksgiving, American culture, and American food ingredients and products. Scope of Requirement The contractor will serve as the single point of responsibility for the successful planning, coordination, production, execution, and closeout of the festival. The contractor will furnish all personnel, supervision, project management, equipment, materials, supplies, transportation, production services, subcontractors, vendor coordination, licenses, permits, approvals, and other resources necessary to deliver a complete and fully operational event, except for any property, services, facilities, or information expressly identified in the solicitation as Government-furnished. Required services are anticipated to include, but are not limited to: Event concept development, design, and planning Venue and stakeholder coordination Project and production management Staging, audiovisual, lighting, sound, and technical production services Event logistics, setup, teardown, and waste removal Exhibitor, sponsor, vendor, and subcontractor coordination Entertainment and programming coordination Food and beverage activation coordination Marketing and promotional support Registration, attendance, and guest-flow management Health, safety, security, and emergency planning On-site event operations and staffing Required licenses, permits, registrations, and approvals Post-event closeout and reporting On-Site Management and Subcontractor Control The prime contractor must provide active, on-the-ground management in Singapore and retain overall responsibility for all subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The prime contractor shall designate an experienced on-site event manager with authority to direct the work, control subcontractor performance, commit contractor resources, resolve operational issues, and coordinate directly with the Contracting Officer�s Representative and other event stakeholders. The on-site event manager must be available in Singapore for required planning meetings, site visits, rehearsals, setup, event execution, teardown, and closeout activities. The event manager must be continuously present at the event site during setup, rehearsals, public operating hours, and teardown. The prime contractor may subcontract portions of the work but may not delegate its overall management, supervision, quality-control, or contractual responsibilities. The prime contractor will remain fully responsible for the performance, conduct, safety, quality, and timely delivery of all work performed by its subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers. The solicitation will require quoters to identify their proposed on-site event manager and provide information concerning the individual�s qualifications, authority, availability, and experience managing comparable events. Quoters will also be required to describe their proposed staffing structure and approach to managing subcontractors and vendors. The final solicitation will contain the complete performance requirements, deliverables, evaluation criteria, quotation instructions, and applicable terms and conditions. Contract and Award Information The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price contract. The Government intends to evaluate quotations and make an award without discussions. Therefore, each quoter should submit its best terms in its initial quotation. Information regarding any pre-quotation conference or site visit, if applicable, will be included in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quotation in accordance with the solicitation, which the Government will consider. System for Award Management Registration Quoters must have an active registration in the System for Award Management at SAM.gov when submitting a quotation and at the time of contract award. SAM registration is free. Prospective quoters are encouraged to begin the registration process early because registration may take several weeks to complete. Registration assistance is available through the Federal Service Desk. Authorization to Perform in Singapore Because contract performance will take place in Singapore, the contractor must be legally authorized to operate and conduct business in Singapore. Unless the contracting officer or grants officer provides a formal notification to the contrary, all Department contractors and recipients must continue to comply with all terms, conditions, requirements and deliveries specified in their contracts or grants. Once a Continuing Resolution or full-year appropriation is signed into law, the Department will begin implementing the plan to orderly resume activity and will notify contractors/recipients at that time. Question 1 � Availability of Kitchen Photographs, Floor Plan, and Government-Furnished Property Inventory (Rephrased from: "Would the Government kindly provide photographs, a floor plan or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas...") The Government is unable to provide photographs, floor plans, or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas due to security concerns associated with the Marine Security Guard Residence (MSGR). The pre-quotation site visit scheduled for August 5, 2026, per Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), did not take place, as no prospective Offerors expressed interest in attending. Offerors must rely on the written description provided in the solicitation, including the Government Furnished Property/Equipment inventory at Attachment 2 ("all cooking pots, pans, and kitchen utensils and equipment as per attached"), together with the Performance Work Statement, to assess equipment adequacy for proposal purposes. Solicitation citations: Attachment 2 (Government Furnished Property), page 28; Section 3, Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), page 47. Question 2 � Minimum Staffing Requirements for the MSG Detachment Cook Position (Rephrased from: "Does the Government anticipate service being delivered by a single on-site cook...or is additional support staff...expected or permitted...") The Performance Work Statement identifies the MSG Detachment Cook as the sole Key Personnel position (Section 4.5.1). The Contractor is responsible for furnishing "all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work" under the contract (Section 1.0, Scope of Work). The Government does not mandate a specific staffing structure; Offerors may propose additional support staff (e.g., a kitchen helper) as needed to fully meet the requirements within their firm-fixed monthly price. Solicitation citations: Section 1.0 (Scope of Work), page 8; Section 4.5.1 (Key Personnel � Position and Function), page 11. Question 3 � Anticipated TDY Headcount Beyond the Standing Detachment (Rephrased from: "Beyond the standing detachment of up to eight (8) Marines, what are the typical and maximum numbers of TDY personnel...") Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services) confirms the Contractor shall provide food services for up to eight (8) MSG personnel and shall accommodate additional Temporary Duty (TDY) personnel at no additional cost to the Government. For planning purposes, Offerors should anticipate a not-to-exceed range of up to four (4) additional TDY personnel during surge periods, beyond the standing eight-person detachment. Because this solicitation is for food preparation services only � and not the procurement of ingredients or supplies, which remains a separate Government-managed process under Section 1 (Prices) � any increase in MSG personnel supported during TDY periods, up to this maximum, will not result in additional cost to the Contractor. Offerors should build sufficient flexibility into portioning and menu planning to accommodate periodic increases above the standing detachment. Solicitation citations: Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services), page 9; Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 4 � Existence of a Budgetary Ceiling for Ingredient Purchases (Rephrased from: "As the Government purchases ingredients from the contractor's weekly shopping list, is there a budgetary ceiling, per-person allowance, or historical monthly spend...") The solicitation does not establish a fixed budgetary ceiling or per-person ingredient allowance. Per Section 1 (Prices), the Contractor provides a weekly ingredient shopping list, which the Government (through the Marines) purchases and delivers to the MSGR. This is a Government-managed process separate from the Contractor's firm-fixed monthly price for labor and services. No historical monthly spend figures are being released as part of this solicitation. Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Prices), page 5. Question 5 � Confirmation of Set-Aside Status (Rephrased from: "Could you please confirm the set-aside status of this acquisition...") This acquisition is unrestricted. No set-aside applies, per Block 10 of the SF-1449. Solicitation citations: SF-1449, Block 10, page 3. Question 6 � Applicability of the Section 5000C Excise Tax (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C applies to this award, or whether a treaty-based exemption may be claimed...") Per the Zadroga Act notice in Section 1 and Provision 52.229-11 in Section 5, payments under this contract may be subject to the 2% excise tax under 26 U.S.C. 5000C unless the Offeror is a U.S. person or qualifies for an exemption. The Netherlands currently maintains an income tax treaty with the United States that may provide a basis for exemption from this excise tax. However, regardless of treaty eligibility, any foreign-person Offeror seeking to claim an exemption must still submit a completed IRS Form W-14 with its quotation. If the form is not submitted, the Government will withhold the full 2% from each payment, per FAR 52.229-11(e)(2). Solicitation citations: Section 1 (Zadroga Act Notice), page 5; Section 5, Provision 52.229-11(e)(2), pages 52�53. Question 7 � Confirmation of Weekday-Only Meal Service (No Weekend Coverage) (Rephrased from: "Please confirm whether any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage is expected...") Per PWS �1.2.2 and Attachment 1, meal service is scheduled Monday through Friday, 0700�1800 hours, on a 20-weekday menu cycle. The solicitation does not require any weekend (Saturday/Sunday) coverage. Service is limited strictly to the five weekday service periods described in the meal service schedule. Justification for Sole Source Market research, including a Request for Information (RFI) posted on SAM.gov under Notice A060703 from 05 May 2026 to 19 May 2026, determined that Charter Communications (DBA Spectrum) is the only vendor capable of meeting the Government's requirement without causing unacceptable delays or substantial duplication of costs. Spectrum is currently the only commercial Internet Service Provider (CISP) with an active, approved Authority to Operate (ATO) and an established physical Service Delivery Point (SDP) presence on Edwards AFB.
